abstract: Xylem cell development is characterized by deposition of a rigid secondary cell wall followed by programmed cell death leading to reinforced hollow tubes enabling water transport and providing physical strength. The molecular network controlling this differentiation pathway is well established, but the early events remain poorly understood. Here, we generated and extensively validated a high resolution, xylem-specific single cell RNA-sequencing atlas of the developing xylem. Subsequent gene regulatory network inference of this dataset identified the transcription factors ZINC FINGER HOMEODOMAIN 3 (ZHD3) and ZHD4 as central regulators of protoxylem development. We show that ZHD3/4 are required for normal protoxylem development and sufficient to trigger protoxylem-like SCW depositions in other xylem lineages by transcriptionally activating the xylem differentiation pathway. This identifies ZHD3/4 as central transmitters of PX morphology and questions whether SCW morphology serves as a valid determinant of cellular identity.
